subject: physics_2
question_text: Three identical resistors are connected in parallel and total resistance of the circuit is R/3. Find the value of each resistance.

verification.note: The mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Paper-II bank the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Transcribed verbatim from the book (p28, VSAQ 17). Hand-checked: with each resistance x, 1/Rₚ = 3/x, and Rₚ = R/3 gives 3/R = 3/x, so x = R — the same answer the book prints.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The parallel rule
lines: Let each of the three equal resistances be x.
For resistances in parallel the reciprocals
steps.margin_note: First mark. Name the unknown x and write the reciprocal sum.
steps.why: Parallel branches share the same potential difference, so their currents add. Current adds means conductance adds, and conductance is 1/resistance — which is why the reciprocals are what you sum.
common_mistakes: Adding the resistances instead of the reciprocals. That is the series rule.

recall.must_convey: That for three equal resistances x in parallel, one by R equals three by x.
accept: one by R equals three by x

steps.memory_tip: Parallel adds reciprocals; n equal resistors give x/n.

steps.label: The value of each resistance
lines: The combination is given as Rₚ = R/3, so
Each of the three resistors has resistance R.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Compare 3/x with 3/R and read off x = R.
steps.why: Three equal resistors of value x in parallel always give x/3. The question states the combination is R/3, so x can only be R.
common_mistakes: Answering R/3. That is the value of the combination, not of one resistor.

recall.must_convey: That comparing 3 by x with 3 by R gives x equal to R, so each resistance is R.
accept: three by x equals three by R
reject: one by x plus one by x plus one by x

steps.memory_tip: Three of them give a third of one, so one of them is R.

insider_note: The trap is the letter R. It stands for one resistor in the answer and appears inside R/3 in the question, so name the unknown x first.
